blocks.text: Top-level domain (TLD) categories are URL categories that give you the ability to group together TLDs for use in the following policies:
You can use TLD categories in policies to control access to domains for a specific country or to block access to TLDs that might be used solely for malicious purposes.

For a transaction, if a TLD matches a custom URL that's linked to a parent category, then it only matches the URL categories (i.e., predefined parent category and custom category) and not the TLD category. For example, if you add .co.jp to a custom TLD category (Japan) and www.yahoo.co.jp to a custom URL category (Yahoo Japan) with the retain parent category option, then the FQDN www.yahoo.co.jp only matches the predefined category (Web Search) and custom category (Yahoo Japan). It doesn't match the custom TLD category (Japan).
On the TLD Categories page (Internet Access > Resources > URL Categories > TLD Categories), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of all configured TLD categories. For each TLD category, you can view:
Name: The name of the TLD category.
No. of Top Level Domains: The number of custom TLDs in the category.
Description: (Optional) Description of the policy rule if available.
The No. of Top Level Domains column displays up to 20 TLDs when you click the number under it. You can view the complete list of TLDs in the edit mode of the TLD category page.

See the maximum limit of custom URLs or TLDs that are allowed and the number of custom URLs or TLDs used in your policies. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.
